Operator:
Good day and thank you for standing by. Welcome to the StellarTech Q3 Earnings Conference Call. At this time, all participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers’ presentation, there will be a Q&A session. Today’s call is being recorded.
I would now like to hand the call over to Alicia Johnson, VP of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alicia Johnson, VP of Investor Relations:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and welcome to StellarTech’s Q3 earnings call. Joining me today are Robert Thompson, CEO; Susan Davis, CFO; Michael Chen, COO; and Emily Carter, CTO.
Earlier today, we issued our earnings press release and presentation, which are available on our Investor Relations website. Please note this call may include forward-looking statements. With that, I’ll turn it over to Robert.

Robert Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Thanks, Alicia. Hello, everyone, and thank you for joining us.

This quarter, we saw meaningful progress across several fronts.

To start, our operating margin for Q3 2024 reached a robust 47.5%, marking a significant improvement both sequentially and against our guidance. This represents a 5 percentage point increase compared to Q2 2024's 42.5% and a substantial year-over-year jump from Q3 2023's 38.5%. This strong performance underscores the effectiveness of our strategic initiatives and operational efficiencies. This reflects a 5 percentage point sequential improvement from 42.5% to 47.5% is primarily attributable to a confluence of factors, including revenue growth outpacing cost increases, efficiency gains from automation initiatives, supply chain optimization, a successful product mix shift, and favorable currency exchange rates. The year-over-year increase from 38.5% in Q3 2023 to 47.5% in Q3 2024 reflects the culmination of sustained efforts to improve operational efficiency and drive revenue growth, leveraging scale efficiencies, strategic cost management, and investment in sales and marketing effectiveness. Last quarter, our guidance for Q3 2024 operating margin was in the range of 44% to 45%. The actual result of 47.5% significantly exceeded this guidance due to stronger-than-expected demand, faster implementation of cost savings, the positive impact of a new product launch, and conservative forecasting.

We also continued to drive improvements through the construction of our new fabs. As previously announced, Fab 1 in Arizona successfully entered engineered wafer production in April, utilizing our cutting-edge 4-nanometer process technology. Initial yields have exceeded our internal projections by approximately 8%, allowing us to accelerate the qualification process for key customers. We anticipate achieving full-scale volume production by Q1 of next year. While Fab 1 is operational, the construction of Fab 2 continues on schedule. We project the fab will begin volume production in 2028, contributing an estimated 18% increase to our overall advanced node capacity. Our first specialty technology fab in Japan has completed all process qualification, and we are on track to commence volume production this quarter. Land preparation for the second specialty technology fab in Kumamoto is progressing as planned, with construction scheduled to commence in Q4 of next year. The groundbreaking ceremony for our specialty technology fab in Dresden, Germany, was successfully held in August. This marks a significant milestone in our European expansion strategy and underscores our commitment to supporting the European semiconductor ecosystem. This supports broader adoption and caters to the evolving needs of the power management and analog IC markets.

Lastly, I want to briefly highlight our P&L guidance for the upcoming fourth quarter. Our revenue outlook for Q4 is projected to fall between $26.1 billion and $26.9 billion U.S. dollars. This range represents a significant achievement and reflects the successful execution of our strategic initiatives and the continued strength of our diversified product portfolio. The midpoint of this range, $26.5 billion, represents a 13% sequential increase compared to the $23.4 billion we reported for Q3. We anticipate a range of 57% to 59% for gross margin in Q4. This guidance reflects our ongoing efforts to optimize our cost structure, improve manufacturing efficiencies, and shift towards higher-margin products and services. Operating margin is expected to be between 46.5% and 48.5%. Where we’ve seen seasonal tailwinds in consumer electronics, momentum in cloud services, and expansion in emerging markets.

Now I’ll hand it over to Susan to discuss the financials in greater detail.

Susan Davis, Chief Financial Officer:
Thanks, Robert, and good day, everyone.

From a financial perspective, we’re pleased with the breadth and durability of our results.

First, our Q3 revenue reached NT$748.6 billion, representing a 12.8% sequential increase compared to Q2 2024's NT$663.6 billion. In US dollar terms, revenue landed at $23.5 billion, surpassing our guidance of $22.8 billion - $23.2 billion issued last quarter. This also represents a 19.5% year-over-year increase compared to Q3 2023's $19.66 billion has contributed meaningfully to our overall success. The strong performance was primarily driven by the continued ramp-up of our leading-edge technologies, specifically 3-nanometer and 5-nanometer nodes. These nodes continue to be the leading revenue generators, with a combined contribution of 67%. Demand from the smartphone segment remained exceptionally strong, accounting for approximately 42% of total Q3 revenue, while the AI/HPC segment emerged as another critical growth engine, contributing approximately 31% to total revenue, up from 24% in Q2. North America continued to be our largest market, accounting for approximately 65% of total revenue.

Second, we saw positive contribution from our utilization rates. The fourth quarter of 2024 saw a significant jump in our utilization rates, primarily driven by the insatiable appetite for compute power in the AI sector. We achieved an average utilization rate of 92% on our 3nm node in Q4, a notable increase from 85% in Q3. Our 5nm capacity also experienced robust demand, reaching an average utilization rate of 88% in Q4, up from 82% in Q3. Which was driven by orders from major hyperscalers and leading AI chip designers, including partnerships with companies like NovaCompute and DeepMind AI for their next-generation AI accelerators.

And although still early, our sales guidance is showing great promise. Our analysis indicates a continuation of strong revenue momentum in Q4 and robust growth for the full year, driven primarily by demand for leading-edge process technologies and explosive growth in the server AI processor segment. We project overall revenue to grow by 28% year-over-year in Q4, reaching $7.8 billion, and a full-year revenue increase of 35% to $28.5 billion. The server AI processor segment is poised to become a significant revenue driver, exceeding our initial expectations and accounting for approximately 16% of total revenue in 2024, translating to roughly $4.56 billion. Is trending positively.

With that, I’ll turn it to Michael for a deeper look at operational performance.

Michael Chen, Chief Operating Officer:
Thanks, Susan.

From an operational lens, this was a solid quarter.

One of the highlights was the operating margin results, particularly in North America and EMEA. In North America, strong demand for our cloud-based solutions and cybersecurity offerings drove revenue growth. In EMEA, the successful launch of our new product line boosted revenue and market share.

Additionally, the sales guidance has enabled more accurate resource allocation and strategic planning. We are revising our 2024 forecast for the server AI processor segment upwards to $4.56 billion, representing a 320% increase year-over-year. This growth is fuelled by the increasing demand for AI training and inference in data centers.

We’re also seeing early traction in our CapEx guidance, where updated processes and strategic initiatives are proving effective. We now anticipate total capital expenditures for the year to be slightly higher than $30 billion USD, representing a moderate upward revision from our previous guidance of $28.5 billion, issued during our Q1 call. This adjustment, representing a roughly 5% increase, primarily reflects accelerated investment in advanced process node development and a strategic expansion of our advanced packaging capabilities, driven by stronger than anticipated demand in the high-performance computing (HPC) and AI sectors. Between 70% and 80%, of the $30+ billion budget will be directed toward advanced process technologies. Between 10% and 20% of the CapEx, or approximately $4 billion, will be allocated to specialty technologies. The remaining 10%, or approximately $3 billion, will be dedicated to advanced packaging, testing, mass making, and other supporting infrastructure.

Now I’ll pass it to Emily for the tech and product update.

Emily Carter, Chief Technology Officer:
Thanks, Michael.

Our product and engineering teams made excellent progress this quarter.

We launched key capabilities tied to the new fab construction progress, supporting broader adoption and technological advancement. Fab 1 in Arizona successfully entered engineered wafer production in April, utilizing our cutting-edge 4-nanometer process technology. Initial yields have exceeded our internal projections by approximately 8%, allowing us to accelerate the qualification process for key customers. Land preparation for the second specialty technology fab in Kumamoto is progressing as planned, with construction scheduled to commence in Q4 of next year. The groundbreaking ceremony for our specialty technology fab in Dresden, Germany, was successfully held in August.

We’ve also been supporting the sales guidance, and are closely monitoring the global supply chain and working with our suppliers to mitigate potential disruptions. We have diversified our supplier base and are building strategic inventory buffers to ensure a stable supply of critical materials and components.

And finally, on the CapEx guidance, our new architecture is allowing for increased investment in our US operations, particularly in Arizona, where we are building a new state-of-the-art fab dedicated to advanced process technologies. The updated guidance reflects an accelerated timeline for the Arizona expansion, driven by the incentives provided by the CHIPS Act.

Let’s now move on to the Q&A.

Q&A SESSION

Analyst 1:
Thanks. Could you expand on the P&L guidance for next quarter and whether you anticipate any shifts in the factors driving your projections?

Robert Thompson:
Certainly. We anticipate continued strong performance in our cloud services division, Nimbus, and are closely monitoring component costs to optimize our gross margin. However, global economic conditions and supply chain disruptions remain potential risks that could impact our actual results.

Analyst 2:
On the revenue results, how much of the growth is attributable to new product launches versus increased demand for existing products?

Susan Davis:
Approximately 60% of the revenue growth is attributable to increased demand for existing products, particularly our 5nm and 7nm nodes, while 40% is driven by the launch of new products, such as our next-generation AI platform and enhanced mobile devices.

Analyst 3:
Could you talk more about the rollout of features linked to sales guidance?

Emily Carter:
We are actively implementing new features to enhance our AI capabilities and improve our manufacturing efficiency. These enhancements are expected to contribute to further growth in our server AI processor segment and support our overall revenue projections.

Analyst 4:
And finally, on the CapEx guidance, is this increased spending expected to impact free cash flow in the short term?

Michael Chen:
Yes, the increased CapEx will likely impact free cash flow in the short term. However, we believe that these investments are essential for long-term growth and value creation. We are committed to managing our capital allocation prudently and expect to see a return to higher profitability margins as these investments come online and contribute to revenue growth.

Closing

Robert Thompson:
Thanks again to everyone for joining us today. We’re proud of the progress we’ve made and confident in our ability to execute in the quarters ahead.

Operator:
Thank you. This concludes today’s call. You may now disconnect.
